answer: The network issues each new agent a cryptographic lantern token whose hash is posted to a distributed meadow ledger; every epoch a random jury of validators selects a small audit sample and requests a proof‑of‑work sonnet that only genuine agents can generate within a tight deadline. If the proof fails, the token is burned and the agent is ejected. An attacker must solve thousands of distinct proofs, costing computational power proportional to the number of fake identities.
